zh-CN.Wood Equilibrium Moisture: Why Humidity: Wood Equilibrium Moisture: Why Humidity History Matters
zh-CN.A research-based explanation of equilibr: A research-based explanation of equilibrium moisture, sorption hysteresis, and why a humidity reading cannot prove that wood is ready for final machining.
zh-CN.Two boards can occupy the same room with: Two boards can occupy the same room without having the same moisture content. One may have arrived from damp storage; the other may be gaining moisture after a dry winter. This article explains that difference using Glass and Zelinka's 2021 Wood Handbook chapter, particularly Equation 4–5 and the discussion of sorption hysteresis on printed pages 4–3 through 4–5. The calculations below illustrate the published equilibrium model. They are not measurements of a supplied board, a drying simulation, or a new laboratory study. Oregon State University's Wood and Moisture Relationships provides an additional explanation of the underlying wood–water relationship.
zh-CN.Equilibrium Describes a Condition, Not a: Equilibrium Describes a Condition, Not a Countdown
zh-CN.Equilibrium moisture content, or EMC, is: Equilibrium moisture content, or EMC, is the moisture content at which wood neither gains nor loses moisture under specified surrounding conditions. It is different from the board's present moisture content. A room sensor measures air temperature and relative humidity; a wood moisture meter estimates a property of the material at its measurement location. Writing down 50% RH does not establish that the middle of a thick board has reached the corresponding EMC. The handbook also distinguishes short surface responses from slower changes through the piece. This is why a delivery date plus an arbitrary number of days is weak evidence for final machining.
zh-CN.Why the Previous Environment Still Matte: Why the Previous Environment Still Matters
zh-CN.Sorption hysteresis means the equilibriu: Sorption hysteresis means the equilibrium relationship depends on whether the wood approached the condition by drying or by taking up moisture. The handbook shows different desorption and absorption paths. A single averaged equation cannot encode all of that history. In practice, ask where the material was stored and whether it recently became wetter or drier. Keep that answer with the readings. It helps explain why two nominally similar boards disagree without assuming that one meter must be broken. Hysteresis is a material behavior; a moisture gradient is a spatial difference within the piece. They can occur together, but they are not interchangeable explanations.
zh-CN.For a fixed air temperature T = 21 °C, e: For a fixed air temperature T = 21 °C, evaluate Wood Handbook Equation 4–5 at h = 0.30, 0.50, and 0.70, where h is RH expressed as a fraction. Define x = K × h. Then EMC (%) = (1800/W) × [x/(1−x) + (K1×x + 2×K1×K2×x²)/(1 + K1×x + K1×K2×x²)]. The temperature coefficients are W = 349 + 1.29T + 0.0135T²; K = 0.805 + 0.000736T − 0.00000273T²; K1 = 6.27 − 0.00938T − 0.000303T²; and K2 = 1.91 + 0.0407T − 0.000293T². The table and chart use this equation and round only the final output to one decimal place. That rounding is for comparing scenarios, not a claim of measurement accuracy.
zh-CN.What the Example Can and Cannot Establis: What the Example Can and Cannot Establish
zh-CN.At 21 °C, moving from 30% to 70% RH chan: At 21 °C, moving from 30% to 70% RH changes the model's equilibrium estimate from 6.2% to 13.1% MC. That difference makes a useful question for a project review: will the finished item experience a similar environmental range? It does not tell us how many days a particular board needs, its actual movement in millimeters, or its internal moisture distribution. The handbook explicitly warns that its tabulated tenth-percent precision should not be interpreted as real precision, and identifies limitations in using the underlying data for scientific model evaluation. Use this as a practical sensitivity example rather than a validated prediction for an individual specimen.
zh-CN.Build a Measurement Record That Can Chan: Build a Measurement Record That Can Change the Decision
zh-CN.For a small furniture job, assign an ID: For a small furniture job, assign an ID to each critical board and mark repeatable measurement locations away from damaged ends and hardware. Record date, room conditions, instrument model, selected species setting, material temperature where required by the meter, and the actual readings. Follow the instrument's instructions for depth, contact, calibration checks, and corrections. Repeat the same locations instead of replacing yesterday's low reading with today's convenient high reading. Use multiple pieces rather than selecting the one that agrees with the desired schedule. If the readings disagree, preserve the spread in the record; an average alone can hide the material that still needs attention.
zh-CN.Turn Observations Into a Machining Relea: Turn Observations Into a Machining Release
zh-CN.Write the release rule before looking at: Write the release rule before looking at the newest readings. It should state the destination conditions, the material-specific target range, how much change is acceptable relative to the instrument's capability, and what happens if readings remain inconsistent. Those are project decisions; this article does not prescribe one universal threshold. Store material with suitable support and exposure to the controlled environment, then recheck after rough machining when internal material becomes accessible. If a critical panel is still changing, postpone its final fit or preserve a defined machining allowance. Keep rough size, finished size, and any later trimming operation separate in the cut list so an allowance cannot silently become a finished dimension.
zh-CN.Separate Solid Wood From Engineered Pane: Separate Solid Wood From Engineered Panels
zh-CN.The sorption equation is not a direct pl: The sorption equation is not a direct plywood movement formula. A plywood layup, adhesive system, coating, and panel construction introduce additional variables. Likewise, a solid-wood movement calculation needs the board width, grain direction, a suitable coefficient, and an intended service moisture range. Do not paste the EMC percentage into a dimensional allowance or treat it as percent swelling. Use the Wood Movement workflow linked below for supported solid-wood scenarios, preserving its input limits and attachment review. Keep panel-specific instructions with plywood work. The useful output of this article is a better environmental and measurement record, not a universal expansion gap.
zh-CN.A Small Follow-Up Study for Your Own Sho: A Small Follow-Up Study for Your Own Shop
zh-CN.To improve a local policy, follow severa: To improve a local policy, follow several identified boards through storage and machining. Keep species, thickness, previous storage, measurement positions, support method, and room history visible in the log. Decide the observation interval in advance and note any changes in heating or ventilation. Compare the time series rather than only the first and last values. Report the number of boards and missing readings if you publish the result. An observation from one board can guide that board's handling; it does not establish a general acclimation duration. The same discipline makes a later disagreement useful evidence instead of an undocumented exception.
zh-CN.Record the previous storage environment: Record the previous storage environment and expected service conditions.
zh-CN.Repeat measurements on identified boards: Repeat measurements on identified boards at the same marked locations.
zh-CN.Apply the meter manufacturer's species,: Apply the meter manufacturer's species, depth, and temperature instructions.
zh-CN.Keep modeled EMC separate from measured: Keep modeled EMC separate from measured wood moisture content.
zh-CN.Use a written release rule and preserve: Use a written release rule and preserve unresolved differences before final fitting.
zh-CN.Can room humidity and a fixed acclimatio: Can room humidity and a fixed acclimation period establish that a board is ready for final sizing?
zh-CN.Room conditions estimate a destination f: Room conditions estimate a destination for moisture exchange. Repeated wood measurements and its moisture history provide the evidence for a machining decision.
